title: Etale locally trivial scheme-action torsor groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G$ a group scheme over $S$ and $V$ an $S$-scheme with a left $G$-action. Use the action groupoid, scheme-torsor objects, cartesian equivariant arrows, and specified trivial-torsor functor of [def-sfb-scheme-action-torsor-groupoids]. An object $(P\to T,f:P\to V)$ is etale locally trivial when there is a covering sieve $R$ for jointly surjective etale families [def-weil-etale-morphism] on $T$ such that for every $b:W\to T$ in $R$ there is an equivariant map $q:G\times_S W\to P$ whose square with $P\to T$ and $W\to T$ is cartesian; equivariance means $q(gh,w)=gq(h,w)$ on every test scheme. Define the etale torsor category $\mathcal T^{et}_V$ to be the full subcategory of these objects in the existing scheme-torsor category, with its actual projection to schemes over $S$, in the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Etale local triviality implies the fppf local triviality already recorded in those objects. Every specified trivial object $(G\times_S T,(h,t)\mapsto h u(t))$ satisfies this etale local condition, by the maximal covering sieve and the cartesian equivariant maps $(h,w)\mapsto(h,b(w))$. The trivial-torsor functor therefore factors through $\mathcal T^{et}_V$ with exactly the same objects and arrows (right translation by the inverse label); this defines its canonical etale version. No stack property or effectivity theorem is asserted in this definition.
